A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study by Chen and Tang. Their main text, algorithms, tables, equations, supplementary material, and proofs support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original Monte Carlo simulations and analyses of leukaemia and lung-cancer gene-expression data, including classification errors and selected-feature counts.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a controlled spike-count sensitivity experiment in Section 7.2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain their whitening, coordinate selection, and discriminant decision rules. The added standard-PCA annotations and optional QDA search-neighborhood discussion provide implementation guidance without establishing a replacement of the stated algorithms.

E1.justification: Section 7.2 adds a synthetic scenario with a two-spike covariance and exactly three nonzero coordinates in each of the mean difference, discriminant direction, and whitened direction. The three original simulation models and both real datasets remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added sensitivity experiment reuses DSDA and the oracle, both already evaluated in v2; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The new experiment fixes the true spike count at two and evaluates assumed counts d = 1, 2, and 3. Existing experimental settings remain, including the 90% variance rule and five-fold CV; newly explained CV details do not establish changes to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Section 7.2 adds a targeted test of underestimating versus overestimating the spike count and examines feature-selection parsimony when underlying sparsity is matched. The earlier strong/weak-signal and covariance-condition-number analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report simulation averages and standard deviations from 200 Monte Carlo replicates. New Tables 13–14 follow the same practice, without introducing additional uncertainty measures, significance tests, or increased run counts.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in shared empirical Tables 1–12 are unchanged. New Table 13 reports 24.19% error for d = 1 and 0.55% for d = 2 or 3. Table 14 reports 3.82 selected whitened coordinates for d = 2 versus 49.35 features for DSDA; the accompanying prose inconsistently says 49.46.

T1.justification: Assumption 2 now explicitly fixes d as n and p grow, and Section 2.4.2 adds an asymptotic computational-cost comparison. The existing theorem statements and proof derivations otherwise remain. Proposition 2 explicitly states Bernstein’s inequality, which v2 already invoked.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain Bayes-consistent classification, competitive empirical accuracy, and dimension reduction through whitened-feature selection. The abstract now highlights QDA optimality already claimed and established in v2; the matched-sparsity conclusion supplies additional support for the retained empirical claim.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes representation dimensionality from raw-feature selection, discusses fixed-sparsity limitations, and interprets the retained dense simulations as performance beyond the recovery guarantees. It also explains spike-count sensitivity and adds computational-efficiency and QDA log-determinant-stability arguments.

D1.justification: v3 discloses freshly randomized CV folds for each replication, minimum-error selection with smallest-s tie-breaking, and the rationale for the existing 1–30 search grid. It also supplies an optional QDA threshold-search center. These additions document implementation rather than establish reruns.

R1.justification: v3 adds Halko et al. (2011) and Feng and Yu (2023) to support its new computational comparison with Lassoed LDA. The broader related-work coverage and research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The revision makes local grammar corrections and adds explanatory paragraphs and remarks. The elliptical-distribution extension moves from Section 5.1 to Section 7.3, and the supplement gains subsection headings; the overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds two sensitivity tables, publication headers, and rearranges existing table placement. The previous asymptotic-order Table 13 becomes Table 15 without substantive display changes. There is no extensive figure or table redesign.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity experiment tests a previously unexamined practical choice, while matched-sparsity evidence and clearer CV and feature-space explanations improve evaluation transparency. These modest gains are tempered by new reporting problems: the optional QDA search center reverses the prior-odds sign relative to Eq. (5.3), and the DSDA feature-count prose disagrees with Table 14. The established algorithms and results remain intact.
